summary.intent: Ship the 0.18.0 release by merging release PR #432 and watching the release run, then find ways to speed up the release pipeline and draft a PR for the best one without merging it.
summary.outcome: Release PR #432 was merged and its run was being watched. The release timing was profiled from the 0.17.0 run (32 min), and a draft PR was committed and pushed on branch ci/release-gate-parallel. It splits a `gate` job out of `release-candidate` so plan and build run alongside verify, saving about 6-7 min. The PR was not merged, and the policy, contract, actionlint and zizmor checks passed locally.

repo: The release workflow (.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) chains plan -> release-candidate -> verify, so the 5.8 min test run blocks plan and builds even though only publishing needs verification.

release-candidate bundles 'identify the merged release PR' with 'verify or recovery-checks succeeded'. Parallelising requires splitting the gate into its own job; execute and version-pr must keep waiting on it.

Two scripts encode the release job graph: .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh and .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-contract.sh. Docs live in docs/architecture/release.md. All must be updated together when the graph changes.

Profile of the 0.17.0 release (32 min wall clock): verify 5.8 min (tests 191 s), builds 3-4.6 min across 5 targets, assemble 1.2 min, execute 2.7 min. The release effectively finishes around minute 28; the remaining jobs are follow-up.
The macOS builds started 5-7.5 min late waiting on runner capacity. That is a GitHub runner queue issue, not something code changes can fix.

The release-pr create/update logic is a 245-line shell script (create-or-update-release-pr.sh). A Rust `release-pr apply` replacement is designed in .claude/plans/DESIGN-release-pr-apply.md but deferred as a maintainability call.
Generated workflows for downstream users such as monokl need `ref: ${{ github.sha }}` on the plan, build-python and execute checkouts (E170).
workflow: The monitor tool cannot run `gh` outside the sandbox, so a background polling script that exits when the run finishes and then prints per-job results was used instead.
Profiling a real release run (0.17.0) rather than an ordinary push run gave the correct baseline for the timing analysis.

Mapping every file that encodes a structure, such as the job graph, before editing helps keep the workflow, policy scripts and docs consistent. Run all checks (policy, contract, behavior suite, actionlint, zizmor) after the edit.
Adding a contract assertion that version-pr needs the gate caught a second path that must not run without verification.

friction: The monitor tool could not run `gh` in the sandbox, forcing a custom polling script.
The first timing script profiled a push run instead of a release run, and timings2.sh had to be written twice.
The auto-mode classifier blocked remote-branch and stash cleanup, leaving it for the user.
shellcheck reports pre-existing info-level notes on the contract script's quoting style, which adds noise when verifying changes.
open_items: Draft PR on ci/release-gate-parallel is open and unmerged. Compare the 0.18.0 release timings against the 0.17.0 table before deciding to merge.

Confirm the 0.18.0 release run finished successfully; it is the first live test of the macos-latest build, attestation --source-ref, single-commit pins, draft-hold and per-publish confirmation window.
`release-pr apply` Rust command is deferred until after the release; its three open design questions are unanswered.
Clean up the bump.rs comments that waited on #454.
Open a wisp-plugins PR with the shell/CI hazard pack, fake-vs-real rule and sibling-sweep step.
E167 (partial forge asset) is unreproduced and fail-closed, so it is left unhandled.
User needs to run the remote branch deletions and `git stash drop stash@{0}`.
Open decisions: whether lock-step workspaces keep `version.workspace = true`, the emoji in the release PR body, and whether to tighten the release-commit manifest check beyond filenames.
